newsitem.title: INDIA: India Deve Gowda says Pakistan talks a first step.
newsitem.headline: India Deve Gowda says Pakistan talks a first step.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said he hoped proposed talks with Pakistan would be the first step towards normalising thorny bilateral ties, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Monday.

"It (talks) is the first step," the news agency quoted Deve Gowda as saying late on Sunday in Bangalore, southern India. "We have to wait for the outcome and later chalk out the future course of action."
Asked whether the two nations would discuss the disputed region of Kashmir, PTI quoted Deve Gowda as saying: "We want mainly to improve relations in the areas of trade, communication and transport."
"I hope that the talks would be a beginning of reviving our relationship," he said.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars since they gained independence from Britain in 1947, two of them over Kashmir. India controls two-thirds of the Himalayan region and Pakistan the rest.
The United News of India on Saturday quoted Indian Foreign Minister Inder Gujral as saying the two nations' foreign secretaries would hold talks later this month.
Gujral said he hoped to hold discussions with his Pakistani counterpart, Gohar Ayub Khan, at a meeting of Non-Aligned Movement foreign ministers in New Delhi in April.
Pakistan said on Saturday it hoped for an early resumption of stalled peace talks with India and was willing to discuss a troop withdrawal from a disputed glacier in Kashmir.
A Pakistani Foreign Ministry spokesman told reporters that Islamabad wanted a peaceful negotiated settlement of problems and "honestly believes in normal good-neighbourly relations".
